utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are you okay to call the case, Madam Registrar? If not, we'll have it skipped.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-98-34-T, the Prosecutor versus Naletilic and Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You sound better than yesterday. I hope you have a speedy recovery. Yes, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I could briefly address the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, by the time that we reached the end of yesterday's proceedings, it was clear to those of us on the Prosecution side that the Trial Chamber as well as the witness himself, Dr. Zujo, would have benefited had photographs of the exhumations and autopsies of Harmandic and Colakovic been available during the testimony. Dr. Zujo referred to the photographs a number of times during his cross-examination, and also in response to questions from Judge Clark. We do have the photographs; and in fact, those were among the 17 binders that were distributed to the Trial Chamber and the parties prior to the beginning of the trial. They were marked as Exhibits P843, for Harmandic, and 844, for Colakovic. Mr. President, I wish I could offer the Trial Chamber an explanation as to why the photographs were not referred to during the direct examination of Dr. Zujo, but I can't. I failed to do it, simply. During the course of the cross-examination and Judge Clark's questions, I recalled that we had the photographs, that we had them marked, and I think all of us on the Prosecution side realised that a mistake had been made. The autopsy photos that were previously distributed are in black and white. We now have a sufficient set, number of sets, of colour copies of the photos. Although he is near the end of his testimony, Dr. Zujo is still here, and will appear in this morning's proceedings. Mr. President, the Prosecution would, therefore, propose to distribute the colour copies to the Trial Chamber and the Defence so that they may be of assistance to the Trial Chamber in what remains of Dr. Zujo's testimony. Although the photographs were provided to the Defence prior to the trial, they were not used during the direct examination and, therefore, the Prosecution would not oppose giving the Defence an opportunity to reopen its cross-examination of Dr. Zujo in respect of the photos should the Trial Chamber wish to do so. If the Trial Chamber permits Dr. Zujo to testify about the photographs, the Prosecution would then propose to tender them into evidence so that they may accompany his Rule 94 bis statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Are those photos the same as the photos in the Document 843 and 844?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, they are the same photographs, only in colour rather than in black and white. And I believe that they are more useful in colour than the black and white copies that were distributed. I should add that the Defence were notified yesterday afternoon after the proceedings that, in fact, the photographs were part of the binders that had been distributed previously, and that we felt that we had made an error in not referring to them during the direct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, Your Honours. I just have a question from the Defence side. We were wondering whether or not the Prosecution would, perhaps, have in their possession copies of the information that had been given to the examining magistrate and the police investigators from the family initially regarding what type of items could be gained from any body that might be found to identify their loved ones. We have not received those. We don't know whether they are in the possession of the Office of the Prosecutor or not. I think the witness indicated he believed they were back in Sarajevo or Mostar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe this question will be asked by the Prosecution if we are going to have this witness here. So we decided to give the Prosecutor another opportunity to ask some questions concerning of those photographs first. And then the Defence counsel are entitled to make their cross-examination concerning with those photos. That is a very limited subject. And after that, Judge Clark will continue her question on that point. It seems to me that has been agreed by both parties. Mr. Usher, would you please bring in the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, at this time we can distribute the colour photographs as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please. Well, these are much better pictures than those in the 17 binders. You may ask questions, maybe one photo after another, so that to tell us what those photos are about.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: That's what I'll do, Mr. President. And I think as everyone probably knows, the witness has not seen these, or at least not recently, and is not aware of the Trial Chamber's decision today. And so it may take a few moments for him to orientate and to refamiliarise himself with them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. Did you have a good rest yesterday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I caught a cold, it seems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You have to be very careful here. Yes, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Further examination by Mr. Stringer:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning. Dr. Zujo, before you entered the courtroom, the Trial Chamber agreed that I would be able to ask you a few additional questions, and perhaps also the Defence, and then we would return to the questions from Judge Clark. And I have a couple of additional exhibits to show you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: At this time I would like to ask that the witness be given exhibits marked as P843 and 844.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Zujo, please take a few moments just to look through these two exhibits, and then I'll ask you some questions about them.

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Zujo, directing your attention first to the exhibit that's marked P843, are you able to recognise this exhibit and if so, could you tell us what this is?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please help me orient myself. I'm looking for 843.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps the usher -- on the very front page, you will find a number in the bottom right-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Zujo, during the course of your testimony yesterday, you testified about the practice of taking photographs both of the exhumation site and also photographs during the course of autopsies performed. Do these photographs appear to correspond to the exhumation and the autopsy of the body that was subsequently identified as that of Nenad Harmandic?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you just a few questions about each of the photographs. So if you will permit me, I would just like to go through each of these one by one. And as you see, there is a legend at the front of the photographs which may be of assistance, or it may not. But in any event, if we could just go directly to photograph number 1, and if you could please describe for us or tell us what is shown in that photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, excuse me for interrupting, Dr. Zujo, it may be preferable or useful if there is an extra set of the photos, we could also put it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Zujo, the photograph that is marked as number 1, are you able to tell us what that photograph shows?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Photograph number 1 is a wider view of the location, the Liska Park, and the location where the exhumations were to take place. You can see a depression there. That is the location. And this was photographed from a wider angle around the location where the exhumation was to take place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this is Liska Park in Mostar; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then photograph 2, and also photograph 3, which appear to be related, can you tell us what those show?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Photographs number 2 and 3 show the location where the exhumation was performed. And do you see the wooden marker with letters "NN", that was just above the spot where we performed the exhumation. You can see it marked with "NN", double "N".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then there's also I see a marker with the letters "LIS", and then the number 5. Does that number 5 correspond to what's called "working number 05" in your report?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, what you see as "LIS", that is the abbreviation for Liska Park.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the number 5, what's the significance of the number "5"?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 5 signifies the number of body, that is, the number of the actual location where we were going to work. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that appear to correspond to the working number 05 that was assigned to the body subsequently identified as Nenad Harmandic?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 5 is the spot which is what I referred to yesterday, this is the number associated with that location, which is the location where we were going to perform the work. And then number 5 was subsequently associated with the body all the way until the body was reburied.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I could direct you now to photograph numbers 4 and 5, if you could please tell the Trial Chamber what is shown in those two photographs.

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Photographs 4 and 5 show clothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Dr. Zujo, in the statement that you provided to the Trial Chamber last October, on page 4 you state that working number 05 was a man's body, overall skeletonisation. The body was wrapped in an army blanket. Are you able to determine or shed any light on whether the blue material is that of clothing or an army blanket? It may be useful just to scan through some of the following -- the later photographs which might shed more light on that question.

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: In photograph number 5, and in the photograph number 4, one can see that it is a military blanket. You see here on the side, you can see it on photograph number 4.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps with the pointer you could point to the location on the photograph that you're -- that you've just referred to.

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This. It would be this portion here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Photograph number 6, please.

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Photograph number 6 refers to the blue jeans.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On number 6, there is also -- it is obvious that there is skeletonised material in the photograph as well. We are seeing parts of the --

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We can see part of the skeletal remains and part of the putrefied matter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I guess, just for the record, it would appear that in photograph 6 we are looking at what remains of the skull and the upper torso of the body, perhaps extending down to part of the pelvic bone; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the photographs that we've looked at so far, 1 through 6, appear to have been taken in the field at Liska Park; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, turning the page to the next series of photographs, it appears, Dr. Zujo, that the remaining photographs were not taken in the field but were, rather, taken at the location of the autopsy examination; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then could you please describe for us what's shown in photograph number 7.

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Photograph number 7 is when the body was laid on the autopsy table. The body bag was open, and a photograph is taken at that point. That is the sequence that is followed during the exhumation, and as I pointed out, this number accompanies the body and is transferred to the autopsy room. And when the bag is open, a photograph is taken in order to confirm that that was the body that had been exhumed at Liska Park.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Dr. Zujo, this photograph gives us an idea or an indication of some of the bones that were used by you, then, to perform your calculations on height. Skull bone, that would appear to be the two femurs, toward the lower part of the body.

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You can see the entire body here. We see the skull, you see part of the ribcage, pelvic bones. You can see femurs, you can see humerus, and you can also see the tibia and fibulas. And also, the putrefied matter that is around the bones.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Photograph number 8, Dr. Zujo, would appear to be the skull?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then there appears to be part of a lower jawbone, perhaps. Perhaps you could tell us what is the bone that is extending from the skull toward the left of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the lower jaw and the teeth in the lower jaw.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Zujo, does this photograph show the fracture, the injury to the lower jaw that you testified about previously?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you can see that I am showing with the knife, I am pointing to the place of the injury on the head.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it appears that the jawbone was actually -- the end of the jawbone was actually separated from the skull. Is that a result of the injury or is that the result of the decaying process that occurred after death?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have an injury to the lower jaw, but it is -- it has also been separated due to decaying process.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the for the record, you've indicated you're the person whose hands, then, are appearing in these photographs with the yellow gloves on?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then photograph number 9, Dr. Zujo, can you tell us what's shown in photograph number 9, please.

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Photograph number 9 shows a fracture of the shoulder-blade and of the -- sorry, no. The collar-bone here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this shows an area of one of the fractures that you've testified about previously?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Number 10, please.

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 10 shows the shoulder-blade or scapula.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is also one of the fractures you've testified about in respect of this body?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Number 11, please.

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a fracture of the fibula.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And one of the injuries which you've testified about in respect of this body. Is number 12 also related -- a related injury?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is also a fracture of the fibula, that is, of one-third of the fibula.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Dr. Zujo, is your testimony that all of these fractures occurred prior to death?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Number 13, please.

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: On photograph 13, we can see the footwear, that is, the moccasin shoe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then number 14.

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: 14 shows the projectile that had been found.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us the other items in 14? Would that be the lighter and the belt buckle?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see much in this picture, this part of the picture.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does photograph number 15 also -- that appears also to show the bullet --

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The projectile, the projectile.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now turning to the next exhibit, Dr. Zujo, Exhibit P844, you could take a moment to look these over. These appear to be photographs associated with the exhumation and autopsy of the body subsequently identified as Aziz Colakovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, unless the Trial Chamber asks me to do so, it's not my intent to ask individual questions about these photographs, and I don't think it's necessary, therefore, to put them on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Zujo, have you had a chance to look through these photographs and do you associate them with the particular examination which performed?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: On photograph number 1, we see a broader view of the Saric Harem cemetery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the additional photographs in this set, do these relate to the exhumation and autopsy of the body that was subsequently identified as Aziz Colakovic?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely. Because as you see here the saponified corpse, and above number 1, you can see that the fatty tissue had been completely saponified so we cannot see the skeleton, which was not the case with the previous body. On photograph number 5, we see a fracture of the 8th rib. And right here, a fracture of the elbow bone. And number 5, as I said a moment ago, fragments of bones have been removed by blows -- by impact in several places. And that's why we concluded it was a projectile.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Dr. Zujo.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Stringer, we saw some hands on the picture 4 and picture 7. Would you please ask some questions to this witness about whose hands are these so as to establish whether the witness was present at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Zujo, are you able to tell us whether you personally are present, shown, are your hands anyway, perhaps you and/or your colleague, Dr. Dobraca, shown in either of the photographs -- any of the photographs that are contained in this set?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are my hands.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is with the yellow gloves?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. President, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any cross-examination, Mr. Par, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Further cross-examined by Mr. Par:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Dr. Zujo. Regarding this photo documentation, I would like to link this with the questions asked yesterday by Honourable Judge Clark, specifically whether it was a criminal investigation or some other kind of exploration. Tell me to begin with who conducted the photographing --

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I had the impression the President had something to tell me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Par, you are entitled to ask any questions concerning with the photographs. But as for Judge Clark's question, we'll give you another opportunity if you have any questions out of Judge Clark's question. You may proceed with your questions concerning with all those photographs at this moment. You may proceed, Mr. Par.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So regarding this procedure of autopsy, who organised the taking of photographs, who conducted it? Who managed this process?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The investigating Judge of the cantonal and county court in Mostar, together with the Prosecutor, had commissioned or engaged the institute for forensic medicine in Sarajevo, as well as the criminal investigations team of the MUP in Mostar, the commission for searching for missing persons was also informed, and the families were informed as well about the oncoming exhumation. And all the photographs that were taken were taken upon the request or on the instructions and orders of the investigating Judge leading the investigation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So who is -- who was specifically the person who was pointing to various locations and saying, Take a photo of this and give me a photo of that? Was it the investigating Judge or somebody else, an expert or something?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as the broader locality is concerned, and the place where we were to conduct the exhumation, it was the investigating Judge who gave all the orders. But the photographs taken in the autopsy room are a different matter. In that case, it was the doctor telling the photographer what to photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So out of these photographs, we are now looking at those of the body of Mr. Harmandic, one of the photographs was taken on the -- on your own orders, and another part of the photographs were ordered, so to speak, by the investigating Judge. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will not go photo by photo. Can we agree that the photographs from the autopsy room, the photographs of the body, were taken on your orders, and the other photographs from the locality were taken on the orders of the investigating Judge? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about photographs 14 and 15, where this buckle or the belt is shown? How about that? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was our job. It was part of our work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Could you tell me now, can you remember at all the specific autopsy conducted on this body of Harmandic, or is it just based on the documentation that you are able to confirm? So do you remember the autopsy itself or can you confirm what you are confirming only based on this background material?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm using the material I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Let me ask you one more thing about the photographs: At some point, there is a reference to this army blanket, and it was -- the identification was not quite clear on photographs 4, 5, 6. It was unclear whether it was clothing or the army blanket. And as far as I understand, you finally accepted the suggestion that it was an army blanket. It is blue. And my question is: Since the army blankets in the former Yugoslavia were usually drab olive or green/grey, have you seen any other bodies wrapped in such blankets, in such blue blankets?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot answer that question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it you who called it an army blanket or was it somebody else? And in your opinion, is it an army blanket or is it something different? Do you have any recollection of that at all?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we said "army blanket," we implied, we meant, that it's not the sort of blanket used in households.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I am particularly interested in this part of the autopsy. Were the bodies all brought to you in those blankets, or was it specific to this body, the body of Mr. Harmandic?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't quite get your drift.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Maybe I didn't phrase it very well. These graves contained certain corpses. So before the exhumation, were all the bodies wrapped in those blue army blankets? Were they UNPROFOR blankets? I'm trying to determine who had placed them there? Was it somebody who had first wrapped them in those blue blankets and then buried them? Or was it in a different way that it all happened? Could it -- was it possible to determine that through exhumation at all?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: We could not see that because we have a lot of exhumed bodies wrapped in blankets, and we were unable to discern any lettering or sign on the blankets which would indicate its provenance from an international organisation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fine. So you just think of it as a blanket different from one as used in households, from normal blankets we use at home. So, let me finish with the blanket. It was your conclusion that it was an army blanket.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. I have no further questions for now, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any cross-examination, Mr. Meek? Further cross-examined by Mr. Meek:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Doctor. How are you?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On Exhibit 844, under picture 5, photograph 5, that would be the Aziz Colakovic issue, I believe you just testified in answer to Mr. Stringer's question that this photograph indicated to you certain things such as fragmentations of bones, and that that is why you, therefore, concluded it was a projectile. Was that your testimony this morning?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, precisely on photograph number 5, you see in the lower third of that a clearly marked elbow bone is fragmented in several places. And if you follow the edge of the ribcage up to the eighth rib, you see that a fragment of the bone has been struck out, removed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, did you testify this morning under oath that this was the reason you concluded it was a projectile which was involved with this body?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: In our conclusion, that is, in the protocol, we wrote that the possibilities were part of a shell or a projectile, things that could have caused this, that is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that conclusion, again, from your testimony yesterday, to make it clear was you concluded it most likely or most probably could have been either a projectile or a fragmentation from shrapnel; correct?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you stand by that conclusion today?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Doctor. In picture number 1 on Exhibit 843 now, there are two depressions in the ground, one to the very left of the photograph and one towards the middle right; correct? Photograph number 1, Doctor.

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: On photograph number 1, you have a clearly drawn location of the depression. Just a second, I want to make this clear. What you see here on my left-hand side, there is a fence that I talked about yesterday. You see a fence, and I don't know distance, the precise distance, of the depression from the fence. And in this part, it was covered with leaves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Doctor, it appears to me on this photograph there are two depressions, one in your lower left-hand corner, and then one towards this -- looks to be like a Mercedes Benz automobile parked along the street. My question is that the grave that we have been talking about is the one closer to the automobile; correct?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the only depression here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you at Liska Park on that day looking for or exhuming bodies of children or babies and then just happened on this body? Is that what occurred?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That day, we conducted exhumations very close to this fence. Newborns had been buried there, new-borns who had died in the maternity ward. And close to that area, we found amputated body parts wrapped into white hospital bed sheets, the kind used in operating theatres. And then we started working on this location marked with number 5.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it by happenstance that you found a location where the body in number 5 was located, or did you have previous knowledge that you should look there for a body?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, I said right at the beginning, that the entire investigation was led by the investigating Judge. I have nothing to do with it. I don't know what we were looking for or why.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. One final question: On that same document, photograph 15, please. Can you tell me, Doctor, was that photograph taken at the scene of the exhumation in Liska Park or back at the location where the autopsy was performed?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yesterday I answered a question regarding the calibre of the projectile, and I said we used the measuring instruments to measure the diameter on the spot. And all of this was done in the autopsy room, photographs 14, 15, 13, all of them were made in the autopsy room. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Doctor, thank you very much. And I wish you a safe trip.

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Par.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would just like to try and correct a mistake in the transcript, if I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] During my examination, I asked on page 16, line 6, a question of the witness to the effect, is it your conclusion that the blanket was an army blanket. The witness just nodded his head but gave no audible answer, so we don't have that answer on the record. And it is my request now that the witness should perhaps answer this question again so that we can have it on the record. Further cross-examined by Mr. Par:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So is it your conclusion, Witness, that in that particular case the blanket was an army blanket?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hope the answer has been recorded now. That would be all. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any re-examination, Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Just one clarification on that last point, because I think it should be clear in the record. Further re-examination by Mr. Stringer:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Zujo, by army blanket, do you mean a blanket of the former Yugoslav army, or as you said earlier a blanket that is of a nature other than one would find in a normal domestic or house setting? Tell us what you mean by "army blanket"?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said a little while ago that it was different from the kind of blankets we use at home. It is a blue or grey without any design, monochrome blue or grey, and in that respect, it is different from the normal blankets we use at home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you mean to suggest -- when you say "army blanket", are you suggesting that this is a blanket that had been used by an army or a military organisation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, with all due respect and understanding that -- from what Judge Clark told me two days ago, or yesterday, this is an expert witness, but certainly his expertise doesn't go to army blankets or that sort of expertise. So I object on speculation. It's a speculative question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, let us exhaust the recollections of this witness to see what his answer is on this particular question. Witness, you may answer the question, please.

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: We called it an army blanket, because it was different from the blankets we have at our homes. That's all I can say.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Dr. Zujo. Nothing further, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Judge Clark? Further questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Dr. Zujo, I think that army blankets have never been known by their comfort but have certainly been known for their longevity, which is proved by the condition of this blanket after so many years under the soil. The photographs have been of great assistance to me, because I think that everybody in the court will appreciate how difficult it is for forensic scientists to estimate an ante mortem height from what literally is a bag of bones. I just wanted to ask you a couple of questions arising out of those photographs. I know it's a very long time ago, and I know that you have conducted many, many autopsies in similar circumstances. If you could cast your mind back to Liska Park, is it a burial place for all categories of faith?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that there are a number of tombstones, some very expensive ones, but I am unable to say whether persons of other faiths were also represented. What I know is that this park is now a cemetery. But I really wouldn't know whether persons of other faiths are also represented there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: So can I read from that that the appearance of the cemetery to you was that it was a Muslim cemetery, a Muslim burial place?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: When you enter the cemetery, among the Muslims, there are markers which you immediately recognise. But if there would be only a tablet there or something like that, a marker, you would have to come close and read what was on it. And I didn't go close there to check on which faiths were there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Perhaps another witness, Doctor, would be able to help us on that. But is there any significance in the Muslim faith to a tablet being T-shaped? Does that have any significance as opposed to a cross, indicating the tablet that you saw that was T-shaped with "NN" on it? Would that be the shape of a marker of a Muslim deceased?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Has no significance.

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it doesn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: The photographs, Doctor, for me anyway, have indicated more than words can, the nature of the horrific injuries sustained by this person before death. The photographs indicate that the fractures were comminuted, fragmented, with total displacement of bone. If a person living, Doctor, had suffered those injuries, the fracture to the collar-bone, the scapula, which is in pieces that you showed us, and the two injuries to the fibula -- I can't see the other injuries -- would that person have been capable of walking?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: All these facts which we found during the autopsy are the so-called isolated fractures. They are severe bodily injuries, but they cannot be linked to the direct cause of death. If you have a fracture of a fibula or scapula, if you have a fracture of the pelvic bone, we can say that overall, these were severe injuries which leads to the traumatic shock, as we call it, and which, could, perhaps subsequently have led to death. But you have a primary injury, which is the injury to the head, which is life-threatening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: In the absence of the injury to the head, do I understand you to say that those injuries could have been led to what is called medically "shock"?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Thank you. I just want to say something to you, Doctor, something I read last night in another witness statement which describes Mr. Harmandic alive as a well-built and very heavy man. Is there anything in bone size that gives anybody an indication that somebody is either a light or a heavy person after death when you are dealing with a skeleton?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could say something about the height based on the bones, but as far as the muscles are concerned and the way the muscles were built, that's something different. Today, for instance, you have a lot of people who are built -- who have a muscular build. They take certain substances to increase their muscle mass. That's something else. But as far as the bones are concerned, in this case, it is clear that we are -- we have here a heavy-built man.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: And then one last question arising out of the questions that Mr. Meek posed to you in relation to the projectile that you described yesterday, is that final photograph in the book of photographs, photograph 15, is that taken among the putrefied body material that you described previously? In other words, if you can recall, is that projectile photographed in situ?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Photograph 15 was taken before the projectile was removed from the body, that is, the remains of the matter. That is number 15. And number 14 is the photograph taken whilst the projectile was already on the table.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Thank you very much indeed, Doctor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Judge Diarra.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. A number of questions I had have been answered already. However, Doctor, I would like to ask you the following: We had a witness here who talked about Nenad Harmandic. He said that he saw him, that he was bloody, had blood all over the body after having been beaten up. And then he saw him, he was black and blue. And then the next day or the day afterwards, his body -- he had -- the volume of his body had increased. Was this the sign of an infection, of gangrene coming before death, and can it have an impact on the speed of decomposition of the body and on skeletonisation?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as the haematomas are concerned, which was part of your question, these are the haematomas which are caused because the damage sustained. And the blood pours out into the surrounding tissue. And it filters out, which leads to the swelling and these particular colouration, blue. This is why we refer to people who have sustained such injuries, that they are black and blue. It -- as it disappears, the colour changes from dark -- black and blue to purple to greenish to yellowish. And this is hat leads to the muscles being swollen. And obviously the skin will also have changed its colour to, as I put it, purple or reddish or greenish. However, it will not have much effect on the decomposition of the body. It may, if it was -- if there was a contagious disease present in the body previously, and then it may accelerate the decomposition. But as far as these injuries are concerned, if the person had sustained them, this will not Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. affect the decomposition.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the -- so the injuries do not have the same impact as a contagious disease?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I have another question. The Prosecutor asked you whether the autopsy enabled you to state that this was the body of Nenad Harmandic. You answered that you were not able to answer that question. Later on, you said that having conducted the autopsy according to the rules, you believe that it is indeed the body of Nenad Harmandic. I am the only one to listen to your answers in French, so I got two different answers, and therefore I'm a bit confused. So at this stage, I do not know whether you're telling us that the body that has been examined, number 05, body number 05, I do not know whether you are telling us that it's Nenad Harmandic's body or not. I don't know if you tell us that it's his body or whether you don't know. So I would like to come out of this room with a clear idea about that. Could you please help me?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The question is: What is the task of the forensic scientist? It is to provide as much information to the family, that is, to also receive as much information from the family about the person that is being sought. And what I have found on the basis of the external and internal examination will then be collated with what the family has provided as information. And you see, not all elements need to dovetail. But if the family says, you see, the age, this and that fits, then I say, this could be a fit because there is a number of parameters there that correspond to the person that you're looking for. But can I say with certainty, this is that body? I cannot do that. I cannot. And the reason is my task is not that is -- this is such and such a person. You can claim it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Doctor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any questions out of the Judge's questions? Yes, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Just one last question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Zujo, I think it would be useful to try to consider your last statement in light of the conclusion which is found in your report. The conclusion states: "After the forensic medical examination with autopsy, and the exhibition" -- and maybe that's the key part -- "and the exhibition and identification of the body, clothing, personal belongings, and objects by the family (Son, Predrag), this male body was identified as the body of Nenad Harmandic, son of Salko, born in 1947." Now, does that remain your conclusion today, as indicated in your report?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Nothing further, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Par.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I have two or three questions Further cross-examination by Mr. Par:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Zujo, there were some questions directed to you from the Trial Chamber whether this was a crime investigation or something else. My question to you is: Had it been a crime investigation, just a regular investigation that you have in the case of murder, would you have given your opinion without having conducted a DNA analysis when you were to -- if you were to have conducted a regular crime investigation?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yesterday, I said that a medical expert completes his task if identification has taken place. So it was not necessary for us to take samples from -- of bones for DNA analysis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll try one more time. Mr. Zujo, you work as an expert in murder cases. And we have a case here. It's the case of Mr. Harmandic. And for our intents and purposes, this is a murder case. You are the expert who is called to testify about the identity of this person, just as you would do in Bosnia and Herzegovina. I'm interested in what the procedure would be in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Is it true that when an expert -- a forensic expert such as you are is engaged for -- in an investigation of the murder case, the investigative magistrate gives the expert a task, and this task is set out very clearly, what is asked of the expert to do. And the expert follows this order and provides the answer to this investigating magistrate. The question is this: Was there such an order? Was there such a procedure in regard of the investigation of the identity of Mr. Harmandic, or was another procedure used?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as the procedure itself is concerned, in the case of Nenad Harmandic, it was the same procedure as for all the other bodies. We had nothing special, because we had an anonymous body until the work was done. It was filed as a John Doe. And as far as the orders are concerned, I could do nothing without the court order. When I went to the Liska, I did not know who I was going to work on. I was just told that there would be an exhumation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fine. I understood you. So it wasn't an isolated criminal case for which a sort of regular expertise was to have been conducted?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The question is: Had it been that way, had it been a case -- just a classic murder case, would you have conducted a DNA analysis? Would you have done it?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Had the identification not been done, I would have had to carry out a DNA analysis. But because an identification was made, I did not do it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll try to simplify it even more --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Par, first I think the question is kind of speculation. Secondly, the DNA test was not mentioned by Judge Clark's question. I hope you could limit your questions within the scope of the questions asked by the Judge Clark.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I understand what you're saying. What I'm trying to do -- I'm not trying to speculate here. I'm trying to get the witness to give us a description of the regular procedure employed in these cases and whether this procedure was done on the basis of a crime investigation, a murder investigation, or something else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I assist you, Mr. Par. DNA is a very expensive procedure, and I don't think in any jurisdiction is it normally carried out when there has been an identification. Similarly in rape cases, if the accused admits to sexual intercourse, then there's no point in carrying out DNA. DNA is only if there is a dispute about identity. So if you put the question very simply to this Doctor, say is it the practice to carry out DNA when there has been an identification of the body?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You heard the question of Judge Clark. Will you please answer it with -- but let me just interject one comment here. Identification that was only made by family members.

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as the DNA samples are concerned, it's a major procedure. If we were to take samples for DNA analysis from all the bodies -- well, let's say in the Visoko municipal cemetery where we have seven to eight hundred bodies who have been identified, but they cannot be reburied until the DNA results have been received, that is, whether they are positive or negative -- had we waited for all these analyses to be completed, we couldn't have conduct reburials. So if the next of kin confirms or identifies bodies. And this is a principal throughout Bosnia-Herzegovina. It is not just in our own institute. It is nation-wide.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand. But I put to you this: If it had not been a regular case, but if the exhumation was done in order to look for missing persons, such exhumations can only be done on the orders of the investigating Judge in the presence of the police. I say to you that such a procedure cannot be done without the presence of the police, the law enforcement, and the crime technicians and the Judge; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But when I go in the field, I don't know what case I'm dealing with. It is a matter of the Court. My task is a medical one. I need to perform an exhumation. I need to perform an autopsy, and I need to stand by what I have found. And it is a matter of the Court to do its job.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I absolutely understand your answer. But what I'm saying is that the court is a proper forum through which this is carried out. And from the documents that we have - I think it's in Tab D or C - this is for the record of the court for which you performed your expertise. And it could be a case against X or Y person, that it is a case of war crimes, and this is part of the investigation with the objective of exhuming a mass grave or a cemetery to identify who is there so that things may be cleared up. And perhaps at some point, this will also be a matter of some criminal proceedings. But this is not any -- case of any specific investigation. In other words, this was done in a framework of some general investigation.

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Listen, I really cannot answer that. Only an investigating judge who has conducted this investigation can answer this question. I am a forensic scientist, and I can only do my job, and it is a matter for the courts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Do you think that DNA analysis would have resolved all the problems that we have been dealing with in the last two days and that we have been asking you as Defence? So do you say that a DNA analysis would have definitively resolved this issue? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as the DNA analysis is concerned -- you cannot quite say this 100 percent, but I have -- my experience is -- in Sarajevo, we had a case -- we had certain items of clothing, and we had all the indications that this was a person that we were looking for. And the answer that we got back was negative. So it may or may not be. The DNA is the best method we have. But is it foolproof? I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions, and I thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness, for coming here to help us. Yes, Mr. Meek. Do you have any questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. President, I only have one or two questions out of Judge Clark's questions, and I'm in your hands whether you want to do it right now or at 11.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, the next witness will be asking for voice distortion, which would require a break in order to set up the equipment. So our request would be to finish this witness now so that the next witness might be arranged before the morning break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: This is also the Chamber's arrangements. So we might sit a little longer for this sitting. You may ask your question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Further cross-examination by Mr. Meek:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Doctor, you just answered Judge Clark's question regarding photograph 15 in Exhibit 843, which is a picture of the projectile taken before it was removed from the body. Do you recall that question and answer, Doctor?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you to look back briefly to picture 7, two pages before that. Now, yesterday, you indicated to Judge Clark's questions that you had really no recollection - and you said this very candidly - no recollection whatsoever of this bullet, particular bullet. So my question to you now: Is there any possibility for you to point out to this Trial Chamber in photograph 7 the location that the projectile in photograph 15, where that was located, if you know?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: On photograph number 15, you -- the projectile is discernible in the vicinity of the bone. Here is the bone. On the right-hand side, you have the long bone. So it's close to the bone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So on picture 7, do you have any independent recollection today of the approximate location of where photograph 15 was taken, or that projectile was located in photograph 7? That's my question.

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't quite understand the question. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I'll try again, Doctor. Photograph 15 is a picture of the projectile before it was removed from the body substance or whatever was left. Photograph 7 is a picture of the body laid out, the skeletal remains laid out on the autopsy table.

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us today, do you have any independent recollection of the approximate location in photograph 7 of where this projectile, the close-up picture in photograph 15, was located, since yesterday you candidly answered to Judge Clark you couldn't even remember the bullet because you have done so many autopsies, understandably?

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that that's what I said, that I didn't remember the bullet. But I stick to the autopsy report which says that we had found a projectile. I said yesterday it was a projectile, but I don't remember the details, where it was turned over to the police team or something. But on photograph number 7, I explained a moment ago that the corpse, once the body bag was opened, was photographed. And it is normal that you don't see the projectile on that photograph because that was the first stage before we started with the autopsy, with the dissection.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Doctor, I understand that perfectly clear. My question is: Can you enlighten me, if at all - and if you can't, please just say so - approximately where was the projectile found in photograph 7? Was it up here on the right, towards the head? Was it down here -- if you know. If you don't know, just say so.

utterances.speaker: HAMZA ZUJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't give you a reply to that question based on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Doctor, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness, for coming to help us. I myself benefit a lot from your testimony. We all wish you a pleasant journey back home. The usher will show you out of the room.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Stringer, at this stage, are there any documents you are going to tender into the evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. It's our understanding that the 94 bis statement of Dr. Zujo, which was filed last October 19th, marked as -- which is now marked as Exhibit 877.1, has already been admitted into evidence pursuant the to Trial Chamber's decision. If that's not the case, then we would certainly tender the 94 bis statement at this time, together with all of the attachments. However, perhaps in light of the decision taken yesterday, those exhibits relating to -- I'm not sure, frankly, how the Trial Chamber wants to handle the Krilic autopsy report. If the decision admitting the report stands, then the reports related to Krilic are still in evidence. And I think the Trial Chamber can decide whether it wants to accept those or not. But certainly with respect to the Harmandic and Colakovic reports, as well as Dr. Zujo's own statement, we would tender that if it's not already admitted. We can withdraw the Krilic, to simplify things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: How about those photographs listed in the Exhibits 843 and 844.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. We tender those exhibits at this time also.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Well, the Trial Chamber believes that we made a decision on the 27th November, 2001, concerning with the statement of that expert pursuant to the Rule 94 bis. But we also believe that this decision has been revoked by the fact that at the request of the Defence counsel and Judge Clark, we called this witness to testify. And there is extensive cross-examinations to this witness. So those documents have to be retendered and readmitted at this stage. Any objections, Mr. Par?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have to object to this proposal because we contest that this particular autopsy identified Mr. Harmandic. We do not believe this kind of material can serve to prove that the body in question belonged to Mr. Harmandic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's my understanding -- and I want for the record to be clear so that I understand it -- the Krilic information in Exhibit P877.1 will either be withdrawn or there will be a new number on that document; is that correct, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I believe they have been withdrawn by the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, we have no objection to the photographs listed in P843 and 844, and we would join in the objection made by Mr. Par.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. At this moment -- yes, Mr. Par? Wait a minute. At this moment, I think the Trial Chamber is in a the position to make a decision on the admission of those documents. Because those documents have already been admitted essentially in the decision made by this Trial Chamber on the 27th of November, 2001. We understand that there are a series of objections from the Defence counsel and it is the subject matter of the dispute in this very case. We noticed that. But anyway, at the request of the Defence counsel, we called this witness, and both parties asked questions to this witness. It is so extensive that we believe that all those documents have the probative value to this case. So we decided those documents have been admitted as the evidence. Yes, Mr. Par.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, on behalf of our Defence team, I should also like to tender the report and finding of Dr. Skavic, which was given a provisional number D2/25, and which we used during the cross-examination of this witness. Yesterday, you ordered me -- you suggested, Mr. President, that if I want to tender this document, I have to attach the accompanying correspondence, so I'm tendering the letter we addressed to Dr. Skavic, which regrettably I did not have enough time to have translated into English. And perhaps I can deal with it in the nearest future. But before we get the translation, I wish to say that in this letter, we asked Dr. Skavic to give his opinion on the findings of Dr. Dobraca. And we provided him with the statements given by the wife and the son of the deceased and this previous witness, Mr. Ajanic, whom we had yesterday. So Dr. Skavic had these three witness statements and the expert report of Dr. Dobraca. And he gave us this reply, the report dated 19th October, 2001. My task is now to tender this. I can do it either now, without the translation, or do it on Monday, as the Chamber decides.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any objections, Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. We object. It's our -- Prosecution submits that the letter opinion of Dr. Skavic is essentially in the nature of expert testimony, which in this Tribunal is governed by Rule 94 bis. That is to say, that expert testimony can be admitted without the expert actually having to come testify, only if certain conditions found in Rule 94 bis are met. The full statement should be Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. disclosed to the opposing party as early as possible, and shall be filed not less than 21 days prior to the date on which the expert is expected to testify. Now, this letter was never provided to the Prosecution, the opposing party, until the date essentially that the Defence sought to offer it into evidence, or at least use it. The Prosecution --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: What is that date?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The date of the letter --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You received it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: We received it yesterday. We had never seen this before yesterday. We have no opportunity to cross-examine the Defence expert, and I didn't object yesterday, Mr. President. I want to be clear, because we do make a distinction. I think counsel is within his rights to consult an expert, to get information in order to assist him in cross-examining the Prosecution expert. And we didn't object to the use of the letter yesterday as an aid or as a means by which counsel could cross-examine the Prosecution expert. But it's our submission that the Defence is now going beyond that and is seeking to tender their own expert testimony without having complied with the terms of Rule 94 bis, and it's on that basis we object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: What's your response, Mr. Par?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My response would be that we are tendering this to demonstrate the tools we have used in cross-examination. We do not intend to call Mr. Skavic in our case to counter the testimony given by expert Witness Zujo. But we are tendering this in order to show what Mr. Zujo referred to, and we intend to fulfill all our obligations we have to the Office of the Prosecutor regarding expert witnesses and expert testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, at this stage, we have to reserve our right to make the decision on this particular matter. And we request the Defence counsel to submit the English translation of the letter to this Trial Chamber as a whole set. And we will make the decisions in this direction. Mr. Stringer, you mentioned that there is some protective measures concerning with the next witness. Would you please inform the Court what are they?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The witness has requested pseudonym, face distortion, and also voice distortion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I guess there are no objections from Defence counsel? So it's granted. We'll have those facilities arranged during the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We are sorry for the late closure of this sitting. I apologise to the interpreters and court reporters and other technical supporters behind this courtroom. And we will resume at 10 minutes to 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: During the break, we looked into the Rule 94 bis concerning with this admission of the expert statement. The Rule 94 bis (c) said that if the opposing party accepts the statement of the expert witness, the statement may be admitted into evidence by the Trial Chamber without calling the witness to testify in person. In this case, we hear the objections from the Prosecution side, so at this moment, we'll give the statement of Dr. Skavic an ID number so that it could not be lost. And later on, during your Defence case, you have the full right to call that witness to this Trial Chamber, and the Prosecutor could have an opportunity to cross-examine that witness. It is so decided. Yes, Mr. Par.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, Your Honour, I would like to correct an error in the transcript relating precisely to this issue. During the break, I was informed by the interpreter that the record on page 37 in line 12, the record misstates that we do not intend to call Dr. Skavic, whereas I in fact said that we did in fact intend to call him. And I want to point this out to the Trial Chamber and to the Registry in order to have this error redressed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Could I ask a question before we go into the next witness, and while we're still talking about the issue which is alive, the identification of the body of Mr. Harmandic. Does the Prosecution intend, or do you have any evidence that will assist us in establishing the location of this burial place, where is it in relation to the Bulevar, to Stela's headquarters, to where prisoners were held, et cetera? It just would help us if we could know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: It's the Prosecution's intention, Judge Clark, to lead evidence of that nature with an upcoming witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And Mr. Scott reminds me, there's also deposition testimony about that in the record which will be brought to the Trial Chamber's attention later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, would you please bring in the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, the next witness, I'm informed, is being assigned pseudonym "ZZ". This witness will testify in reference to paragraph 7, 10, and 11 of the indictment, the background section; also superior authority of the accused Naletilic under paragraphs 14 and 16; general allegations, 18 through 21. The Witness will testify in respect of paragraphs 26 through 29, 31, 33, and 34, the persecution count. Also, in respect of counts 2 through 8 regarding forced labour of detainees. The witness will testify in reference to paragraphs 37 through 39. And finally in respect of counts 9 through 12, the witness will testify in reference to paragraphs 45 and 50.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I can inform the Trial Chamber that we will be asking the video -- the technical booth to play two short videotapes during the course of this witness's testimony, one of which is footage that the Trial Chamber saw previously of the Vranica building, only, as you may recall, part of that in reference to a question from the Trial Chamber, now a fuller version of that footage is being provided in response to a request from the Trial Chamber, and with the audio and a transcript of the audio will be distributed at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. That has been arranged already, right? Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration in accordance with the paper the usher is showing to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please. Examined by Mr. Stringer:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, good morning. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: Yes, I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I can inform you that the Trial Chamber has granted your request for protective measures. For the purpose of your testifying in these proceedings, you are being given a pseudonym, pseudonym "ZZ", and I ask you not to mention your name or give other information about yourself that will identify you during the course of your testimony this morning. Also the protective measures of facial distortion and voice distortion are also in effect in order to protect your identity. Now, before I start asking you questions, there's a piece of paper that I want you to look at. On the piece of paper, you should find your name, your real name, as well as your date of birth. Together with the pseudonym "Witness ZZ." And I would ask you to look at the paper, without saying your name, just inform the Trial Chamber whether the piece of paper correctly identifies you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, in May of 1993, were you a Bosnian Muslim living in the city of Mostar in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in February of 1993, did you join the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and were you a member of the military police, of the Armija?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you stationed at the Vranica building headquarters in the city of Mostar in -- particularly in West Mostar in May of 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I would ask you at this time if you could briefly inform the Trial Chamber whether the Vranica building was attacked on the 9th of May, 1993, and how long you remained in the Vranica building after the attack began.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: On 9th of May, after the attack, we stayed in the Vranica building for approximately 36 hours, and we were captured -- that is taken prisoner -- on the 10th of May by the HVO soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Prior to your being captured by the HVO soldiers, before you left from the Vranica building, did you and some other members of the Armija change out of your uniforms and into civilian clothes? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you tell us what happened, then, after you exited the Vranica building with the other -- your other colleagues in the Armija?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: When we came out, we were lined up in front of the school of economics, and the elderly, the women and children, were separated onto one side, and men ages 15 to 50 approximately were placed on the other side. One part went to the Velez stadium near Bijele Brijeg, and a group that was suspected to have been consisted of members of the ABiH was taken in front of a ministry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then were you one of the people who was taken to the area in front of a ministry?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, briefly, then, what occurred while you were in front of this ministry?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: We were lined up in front of this ministry. We were surrounded by a large number of the HVO soldiers and a number of men who were part of Tuta's guards. And then Tuta came in. He said that we were supposed to fight together, how we had betrayed the city, and so on. That's that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, at this time I would ask with the assistance of the technical booth, if we could dim the lights a little bit and play the videotape which has been marked as Exhibit P17.1. Before we do that, I've given the registrar a transcript of the audio portion of the tape for distribution at this time, which has been marked as P17.2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you're a protected witness, so the first time we look at this videotape, I don't want you to say anything.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: If we could just stop it for a moment, please. I don't know that we've gotten copies yet into the translation -- interpretation booths, which is a failure on my part.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I guess we are ready to roll the tape, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: This first group of 12 proves how this conflict was planned and conceived by Muslim and Serbian policy; namely, their soldiers say in this manner, the intent has been to join the line Konjic, Jablanica, Breznica, Stolac, Mostar, which would then be controlled by the BH army. Today's operations successfully severed that chain. There were about 70 extremists. They surrendered with the civilians. They changed into civilian clothes, threw away their rifles in the hallways and surrendered together with the civilians, the Croats that they had held as hostages. They mistreated our people. Forced them to put out fires in the hallways and such. The operation was successful, though. There were injured and wounded but none on our side. There were none, not this time. This commander spoke to another group of Muslims, the one that attempted to conceal their treacherous travel by changing into civilian clothes. Several months ago some of them had fought with the Croats against an Serbian aggressor. The question remains on which side they were even then [as interpreted]. Well, no one expected they would do it, that they would turn against the Croats. The HVO soldiers say it is quite indicative that not a single Serbian shell had fallen on the city in the past seven days.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: If we could go back to a portion of the videotape in which a line of men wearing civilian clothes is shown, if you could keep moving back from there. Okay. Stop, please. Mr. President, could we go into private session, please, for just a few moments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, the location of the video footage of these men wearing civilian clothes, can you tell us, if you know, the location where this footage was taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: This is in front of the ministry building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think we can take the video off the screen now. And, Witness, let me ask you whether, then, you said that you were at the ministry area. Were you and others, then, taken to a different location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: Yes, they bussed us to the MUP station in Listica, which is Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you remain at the MUP station in Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: I don't know the exact dates, but it seemed something like between two and three weeks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
