utterances.text: Are you able to recall approximately how many prisoners were in your group that were held there at the MUP station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: There were between 50 and 60 of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you describe for the Trial Chamber generally the conditions of your detention at the MUP station during those two to three weeks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: There were two small rooms, approximately 4 to 5 square metres, and 25 to 30 men were held there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So are you saying there were 25 to 30 men in each of these two small rooms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. President, with your permission, we would like to show the next piece of videotape which is marked as Exhibit Number 30. And as that's playing, Witness, if you're able to recognise anything or make any comments, please feel free to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I should ask, are we at the beginning of the videotape? Did we start at the very beginning?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: If I can assist, I think we can stop right there and begin to roll it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, while we're looking at this, could you just tell us if you recognise this place, and if so, what is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: Yes, this was the MUP station in Listica, or Siroki Brijeg, apologise. This is the staircase leading down to where the cells were. This is one of the cells except these mattresses were not around at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it your testimony that 25 to 30 men were in each of these cells?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. Yes, that's the other cell.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. Mr. President, I would like to just very quickly show three photographs to the witness. They are already in evidence. Exhibit 26.6, 26.7, and 26.8.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could I just ask you to take a look at each of those photographs and then to tell us if those are locations which you have just identified in the videotape.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: Yes, those were the locations. That's the place leading down to the cells.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And perhaps looking at the other two photographs, if you could tell us, please, which of the cells you were kept in.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: I was in both of them. At first, I was in this first one, and then later on, they transferred me to this one here. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First you were in the cell that has the green -- the green blanket, I see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, how did the prisoners sleep in these cells during the two to three weeks that you were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: We slept in such a way that we agreed that some would sleep and others would stand up, and then we would take turns.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived at this location in Siroki Brijeg, did you encounter any other prisoners who were there before you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: Only one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall who that was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: If I recall correctly, it was -- he was a commander of Blagaj Brigade, in the ABiH.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, during the two-to-three-week period that you were detained at the MUP station, did you receive any beatings? And if so, could you describe that to the Trial Chamber, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: Yes, they beat me first when we had just arrived. A person entered the room and just started beating us at random. And he hit me with a butt of his pistol in the head. Several days later, another man came who was taking us out of the cell one by one, and again, we were being beaten.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall the name of any of the people who beat you when you were at the MUP station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: One was Romeo Blazevic, and the other one I heard being called by others Cikota, but I don't know his name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know either of those people from before the conflict had started?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: Yes, I had known Romeo from before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you know him, if you can say in what -- how did you know him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: Well, I had heard of him, and I knew him by face. I knew how he looked. I also heard that he was a petty criminal in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, during the time that you were detained at the MUP station, were you and other prisoners taken to work at a swimming pool location in the area?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I believe we've gone way beyond background, and I am objecting now to leading and suggestive questions. I didn't on the last one, but if it's going to continue I must raise these objections to the leading and suggestive. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Stringer, it is a leading question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I agree, Your Honour. I'm trying to move a little quicker and I'll rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, during the time that you were held in Siroki Brijeg in the MUP station, were you taken out to perform labour?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: Yes, I was taken out to some pool.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you taken to any other locations or just to a pool?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: While I was in Siroki Brijeg, we only worked at the pool.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: At this time, I'll ask the witness be shown two photographs, Exhibit 26.9 and 26.10. Perhaps we could put 26.9 on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, if you recognise anything shown in either of those photographs, could you inform us and tell the Trial Chamber about that, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: That is the pool where we worked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you just -- could I ask you to take the pointer and to show us specifically what area you're looking at.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: This one here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And then in the next photograph, are you able to recognise that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: Yes, that is the pool.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could I ask you to just quickly take a pen and put a circle around the swimming pool which you've indicated in Exhibit 26.9.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Now, when you and others were working at this location, were you under guard? Were there guards present?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to recall what unit these guards belonged to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: I think that they were part of the Tuta's guards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber, please, why you believe that they were Tuta's guards, or why you associate them with Tuta?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: Because there was a man who had worked with me who was in the same unit, and he had recognised the man who, as I heard -- for whom we had worked, his name was Jablanica. And I had also heard that he was a deputy commander in Tuta's guards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the time that you worked at the swimming pool, did you observe any beatings of prisoners take place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: Yes. That man who used to be in the Tuta's guard before, he was the one who was beaten.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, could we briefly go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, looking at those two photographs, are you able to recognise anything about them? And if so, could you tell the Trial Chamber, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: Well, this is Heliodrom, the building where we were held. Some more construction has been done since on it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking first at Exhibit 20.2, which is -- I believe it's on the ELMO, Witness, I would ask if you can recognise the building where you were held. If you could place a circle around that, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And while you've got the pen in your hand, if you're also able to do the same thing for the other photograph, Exhibit 20.11.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, a couple moments ago you mentioned that you were wounded on the 16th of August. So let me ask you some questions about the period in between your arrival at the Heliodrom in June and the date of your injury on the 16th of August. During that period, did you perform any labour? Were you required to perform labour? And if so, could you inform the Trial Chamber of the locations in which you performed labour.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: First, the first few days of our stay there, we worked only in the area surrounding the Heliodrom. We did the cleaning, dug trenches, made bunkers, and so on and so forth. And later, a couple of weeks later, they took us to the town of Mostar itself where we worked mostly on the front lines, dug trenches, constructed bunkers, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall the names of the places in Mostar, in the town of Mostar, in which you performed labour?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: Well, those were Podhum, the Avenija itself, the primary school, the high school, the Santic Street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were wounded on the 16th of April -- excuse me, 16th of August, where did that take place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: That was in Santic Street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell the Trial Chamber, please, how you were wounded and the conditions there on Santiceva Street at that time and generally when you were working in that location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: Well, while we were working there, it was always possible for shooting to start. We were making trenches and protection walls made of sandbags. And one day, we were working making a bunker. I was making the roof, putting a plank on the top of the bunker. And at that moment, I was wounded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were detainees on Santiceva Street ever used as human shields?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did that happen to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: Yes, it did. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you describe for the Trial Chamber, please, the manner in which you were used as a human shield?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: We were lined up in front of the line, and they shot from behind our backs at the members of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far away was the -- were the members of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: Well, approximately 5 or 6 metres was the distance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the members of the Armija return fire on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: No. For the most part, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, coming back to your injury on the 16th of August, were there other prisoners who were also wounded on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: Yes, another young man was wounded at the same time as I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, at this time I have three documents to show the witness. Two of them are new exhibits, and we have those ready for distribution. Those are Exhibits P565.1 and Exhibit P566.1. And in addition, we would ask the witness be shown Exhibit 774, which has already been tendered into evidence. And I think that in order to speed things along, and also to continue to protect the identity of the witness, perhaps we can all work with the document without placing it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, now, do you have a document in front of you that has been marked -- I'll just wait a minute until the copies have been distributed. Okay, Witness, now, I have just one question referring first to Exhibit 565.1, which is dated the 16th of August, 1993. If you turn to the first page, the English translation version, you'll see the -- it's the document I think that you just... Yeah. The exhibit number is on the very first page, and then the second page will be the original language B/C/S version. So if I could ask you to turn to that, and is this a document that's dated the 16th of August, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you see your name appearing on that document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. Moving next to Exhibit P566.1, is this document dated the 19th of August, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you see your name on that document as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, moving, finally, to the third exhibit, which is Exhibit 774, which is the one on your right -- yes, that's it. If I could ask you to go through that document, turning to Item Number 94, please. The document consists of a number of numbered items, and if you could go to Number 94.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: I found it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see your name on that document as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do these three documents, Witness, appear to relate to the wounding that you testified about on the 16th of August, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, if I could just ask you to then next to Item Number 122, which I believe contains a reference to the name of Neno Harmandic. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that name mean anything to you, "Harmandic"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, thank you, Witness. You can put those documents aside now. I have just a few remaining questions. You've testified already about having seen Mr. Naletilic in Siroki Brijeg. Did you ever see this person on any other occasions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: Yes, at the Heliodrom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber, please, approximately when that happened and describe the location and the other circumstances of that occasion when you saw him in the Heliodrom.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: Well, I don't know the exact date, but it was in the first weeks of our stay at the Heliodrom. Mr. Naletilic arrived with his bodyguards and entered the building of the prison.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is the building that you've just referred to, is it shown anywhere on either of the two photographs which you've already marked from the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: Yeah, I made a circle around them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So then are you referring to the same building in which you were held during the time that you were at the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you when you saw Mr. Naletilic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: In the room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he inside the building, was he inside the room, or did you see him through a window?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: No, I saw Mr. Naletilic only through the window. I only saw him entering the building, nothing more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, during the time that you were working on the frontline positions in Mostar, did you encounter any members of the Croatian army, that is, the HV?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: I cannot say for sure, but I think I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber, please, why you think so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: Because they were talking in a dialect which is not typical of Mostar or the surrounding area. Some of them had a Dalmatian accent actually.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, it is my understanding --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: If I may be permitted, Mr. President, I just have a couple more questions which relate to the remainder of the witness's time before he was released.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, it's my understanding that after you were wounded, you were taken, then, to a hospital in West Mostar, and that you remained there until approximately mid-September of 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that from the hospital, you were returned to the Heliodrom complex where you remained for another 10 to 14 days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that after that 10 to 14 days, you returned to the hospital, and that you remained there until shortly before the time you were released in March of 1994. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that you were able to remain in the hospital for that period of time because of the assistance of others who helped to sort of hide you in the hospital. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I think we'll break here. Mr. Usher, would you bring the witness out of the room after pulling down the blinds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we'll adjourn until 9.30 Monday morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
